text:
mira: heads-up: saw weird timeline on the short-seq microbenchmark this morning — GPU kernels idle spikes between batches, looks like a serialize on kv read path
jonathan: ugh, saw that too on friday. had a hypothesis that our kernel selector prefers fused-attn for <48 tokens which forces extra memcpy?
sam: can you paste the perf trace? nvtrace from the repro run would help.
mira: attaching snippet from the NVTX timeline (trimmed):
```
CPU: enqueue batch (0.8ms) -> memcpy H2D (1.2ms) -> kernel launch (0.05ms) -> wait (3.4ms idle) -> kernel resume (0.04ms)
GPU: fused_attn_forward (0.9ms) | kv_read memcpy (2.8ms) | flash_attn_variant (0.5ms)
```
lee: that wait is suspicious — looks like host-side memcpy for KV interleaving is blocking queue. If the batching heuristic breaks contiguous KV buffers we get many small memcpys and stalls.
jonathan: confirmed: when batching mixes different context lengths we end up with scattered offsets => cudaMemcpyAsync falls back to synchronous path on our stream because of pinned buffer ownership.
ops-bot: perf alert: regression +12% p50 latency on short-seq path since rollout 2026-03-07 03:00UTC
mira: repro script I ran (shortened):
```
# repro: 8 concurrent requests, seq lens [8,12,6,10]
python repro/bench.py --model oracle-fused-4b --batching window=50ms --kv-layout=interleaved
```
sam: tried `kv-layout=contiguous` and the idle gaps disappeared. timeline: memcpy aggregated once per batch. p50 back to baseline.
jonathan: That suggests two levers: kernel selection (fused vs flash) and kv layout. If fused-attn expects interleaved KV, we pay multiple small memcpys. Flash-attn variant can operate on contiguous KV with a single copy.
lee: action items: 1) add a fast-path in batching planner to prefer contiguous KV for short batches, 2) make kernel selector consider expected memcpy count (cost model), 3) add a perf test for mixed-length microbatches.
mira: agreed. I'll prototype change 1 in batching planner — basically coalesce per-request KV allocations into single contiguous slab when total tokens < 64.
jonathan: for (2) we can model memcpy cost as alpha + beta * bytes and estimate kernel runtime + memcpy-time for each candidate; if fused-attn saves compute but triggers N memcpys it may lose.
sam: can we get more metrics from device side? nvprof counters show PCIe bandwidth usage spikes during stall windows — implies we're saturating host<->device copying. I'll run a nvprof job with pci counters and upload.
mira: pasted nvprof snippet:
```
Device-to-host bytes: 0
Host-to-device bytes: 1.9GB over 60s
Peak PCIe util windows: 9.2ms spikes aligned with short batch arrivals
```
ops-bot: note: rollout tag `fused-opt-2026-03-05` is the last change touching kernel choice rules.
lee: timeline for fix? if we add planner change (coalesce small kv copies) that's low-risk and should be revert-safe. we can gate it behind a config flag and run canary on a few tenants.
jonathan: I'll sketch the selector change and the cost model tonight. maybe we can add a unit that simulates per-batch memcpy count using current buffer layout heuristics.
sam: also add perfetto traces for the canary to capture user-visible tail latencies; include memcopy histogram and kernel gaps.
mira: I'll open a short PR for the batching planner change + test, target MR today. PR will include perf graphs (before/after) for the repro script.
lee: great. add a TODO for long-term: explore zero-copy KV for small seqs or persistent pinned pools to avoid fallback sync.
jonathan: noted. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
sam: ping me once PR is up, I'll run the nvprof/pci counters and validate.
mira: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/+/12345 — includes repro, perf graphs, and config flag `planner.coalesce_kv_short_batches=true`
jonathan: merging plan: canary to 5% traffic for 24h, watch p50/p95 and PCIe util metrics. revert if regressions.
lee: adding to oncall checklist.
mira: closing loop: initial canary looked good — p50 -8%, PCIe util spikes reduced. will follow up with thorough perfetto capture tomorrow.
sam: uploaded nvprof + perfetto traces to the megastore: /perf/traces/1780001234/ — added labels `kv-coalesce-try1`
lee: excellent work. saved us from a weird tail regression.
jonathan: lesson: kernel choice must include host-side copy costs in the heuristic. small compute savings can be erased by IO patterns.
mira: yep. filing a follow-up to include memcpy cost in the selector's cost model (ticket INF-8623).
ops-bot: ticket INF-8623 created by mira (priority P2)
